results.title: What satellites see vs what pastoralists know: A mapping story from the Karamoja Cluster
results.description: This carousel tells the story of how mapping for climate resilience and peace works best when satellite data is combined with local knowledge. Focusing on the Karamoja Cluster across Uganda, Kenya, South Sudan, and Ethiopia, it shows why understanding mobility, drought, and resource tension requires seeing beyond what remote sensing alone can capture. The carousel walks through a two-phase mapping process: first, large-scale remote mapping using satellite imagery and machine learning, and then participatory mapping with local communities to fill critical gaps. Pastoralists helped identify missing buildings, seasonal resources, and local realities invisible to satellites. The result is a richer, more accurate dataset that reflects how people actually live and move. The key message is that maps shape decisions about aid, services, and investment, and without grounding data in lived experience, even well-designed systems can fail

results.title: Perfil del proyecto: Fortalecer el sector ganadero mediante la construcción y dotación de una planta productora de sal mineralizada en San Vicente del Caguán
results.description:
En el marco del Grant GIZ–CIAT 81310949 y con aportes del Scaling for Impact Program del CGIAR, se desarrollaron nueve perfiles de proyectos orientados a impulsar modelos de ganadería sostenible y libre de deforestación en las cadenas láctea y cárnica. Asimismo, contó con aportes de los Acuerdos Cero Deforestación y con el apoyo del proyecto UK PACT – Transformando las cadenas de suministro hacia un futuro libre de deforestación, implementado por la Alianza de Bioversity International y el CIAT, así como con el respaldo de los contribuyentes al Fondo Fiduciario del CGIAR.

Estos perfiles ofrecen una hoja de ruta para la estructuración y gestión de proyectos de inversión pública y privada, dirigida a empresas del sector, el Ministerio de Agricultura, ONG y entidades firmantes de los Acuerdos Cero Deforestación. El proceso metodológico incluye: análisis de contexto y políticas, identificación de mecanismos de financiamiento bajo un enfoque de cadena de valor, definición de líneas de inversión en sostenibilidad y gestión de proyectos ante fuentes de financiamiento.

Los perfiles, elaborados en marco lógico, integran diagnóstico, alternativas de solución, objetivos, indicadores y estrategias de implementación, consolidándose en lineamientos técnicos y prácticos para fortalecer capacidades en la formulación de proyectos hacia una ganadería sostenible y libre de deforestación.

They also received contributions from the Zero Deforestation Agreements and support from the UK PACT project – Transforming supply chains toward a deforestation-free future, implemented by the Bioversity International and CIAT Alliance, as well as backing from contributors to the CGIAR Trust Fund.

These profiles provide a roadmap for structuring and managing public and private investment projects, directed to sector companies, the Ministry of Agriculture, NGOs and entities signatory to the Zero Deforestation Agreements. The methodological process includes: context and policy analysis, identification of financing mechanisms using a value-chain approach, definition of investment lines in sustainability and project management for financing sources.

results.title: Resilient Seed System Development for Community Seed Banks in Western Kenya
results.description: Ensuring the availability of high-quality and healthy seeds, particularly the neglected and underutilized species (NUS) remains a critical challenge in effective agrobiodiversity conservation and utilization to enhance resilient nutritive food security. The formal seed sector largely concentrates on a limited number of crops, leaving gaps in farmers’ access to diverse and farmer-preferred resilient crop varieties. The national and international partners, namely the Alliance- Bioversity International & CIAT, the Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) and the local county authorities devoted concerted efforts to support establishment and development of community seed banks in western Kenya. The International Center for Agriculture Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) joined the program in 2023 under the CGIAR Nature Positive Solutions Initiative and continues under the Multifunctional landscape scientific program of the same. The ICARDA intervention focused on development of (1) a farmer-friendly variety catalogue, (2) early generation seed production manual, (3) provision of post-harvest seed operations equipment and facilities, and (4) the necessary capacity development to maximize the benefits from the facilities. The purpose of the Support to Resilient Seed System Development for Community Seed Banks in Western Kenya was to strengthen the functionality and sustainability of community seed banks in Kisumu and Vihiga Counties through capacity building, equipment upgrading, and demonstration of improved seed production and post-harvest practices. Specifically, the visit’s aim was to ensure effective utilization of post-harvest seed processing equipment, enhance the technical skills of CSB members, and support the implementation of demonstration activities that promote quality seed production and dissemination under the CGIAR Multifunctional Land Scape Science program building on the achievements of Nature Positive Solutions Initiative investments. This first Technical Support and Capacity Development under the MFL program was carried out from 26 to 29 August to kickstart the program’s follow-up process. The mission focused on (1) upgrading of post-harvest seed operation equipment provided under the N+ initiative, (2) training Community Seed Bank (CSB) members, and (3) designing and implementing demonstration activities on crop catalogue and EGS production manual enhancement. This report summarizes these activities.

results.title: Regional multi-stakeholder workshop organized by IRRI on potential pathways for methane mitigation in Southeast Asia’s rice sector held in the Philippines
results.description: The three‑day regional workshop held in Makati City, Philippines, marked the launch of IRRI’s AcceLER project, bringing together delegates from Cambodia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Viet Nam, with observers from Indonesia, Lao PDR, and Malaysia. The event centered on accelerating methane‑reducing rice practices across Southeast Asia. Workshop discussions highlighted the need for accessible and scalable climate‑smart practices, emphasized in opening remarks by Philippine Agriculture Undersecretary Christopher Morales. Participants worked on shaping national methane‑reduction roadmaps, targeting a 15% decrease in rice‑sector methane emissions by 2030. Sessions focused on strengthening Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems, including remote‑sensing tools, to improve data accuracy for national climate commitments. IRRI scientists underscored the importance of robust MRV and evidence‑based data for achieving NDC targets. The workshop also explored regulatory gaps, technologies influencing emissions, and opportunities for climate financing and carbon markets, fostering collaboration toward low‑emission rice production in the region.

results.title: Direct Seeders: Reducing Labor, Ensuring Timely Field Operations, and Mitigating End-of-Season Drought in Mali
results.description: Direct seeders are mechanized tools designed to plant rice seeds directly into prepared fields, bypassing traditional transplanting. This innovation reduces labor requirements, saves time, and ensures that field operations are completed promptly, which is critical for crop establishment. By enabling timely planting, direct seeders help mitigate the impacts of end-of-season droughts, improving crop survival and yields. They benefit smallholder farmers in Mali by enhancing efficiency, supporting sustainable production, and increasing resilience against climate-related stresses.

In Ethiopia, these activities were supported by the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR) bean program and implemented in collaboration with multiple partners, including EIAR, EIAR/SAA, and the Hawassa and Jimma Agricultural Research Centers. The varieties promoted included SER119, Awash 3, Key Wolayita, Key Bure Miten, Tafash, and SER125. As a result a total of 83,342 (34,933 women) farmers have been reached. In Tanzania demo plots were established in collaboration with Farm Africa in Manyara region. Farmers were also linked to seed sources.
In Uganda, recently released biofortified and climate-resilient bean varieties, as well as non-varietal climate-smart innovations, were showcased during the World Food Day celebrations at Rwibitaba ZARDI.In Tanzania and Uganda, the demonstrations mainly focused on promoting newly released bean varieties.

results.title: A roadmap for solar irrigation expansion in Ethiopia
results.description: The project builds on five years of successful work in South Asia, where it proved that solar-powered irrigation helps farmers depend less on rainfall. The second phase of the project moves beyond irrigation to introduce a wide range of solar technologies such as cold storage, dryers, milling and agro-processing equipment that will help farmers lower production costs, keep their harvests fresh longer, reduce waste and create additional ways to earn an income. This holistic approach is designed to transform agricultural practices and improve the livelihoods of farmers.

results.title: Strategic advancement meetings conducted to evaluate promising crop varieties for farmers in West Africa
results.description: CGIAR's Accelerated Varietal Improvement and Seed Delivery of Legumes and Dryland Cereals in Africa initiative organized strategic meetings in Mali and Nigeria to evaluate the progress of new crop varieties through a systematic stage-gate process. These meetings brought together experts to assess groundnut, pearl millet, and sorghum varieties at critical decision points, determining which should advance to the next development phase based on performance data, farmer needs, and market potential. The disciplined evaluation process ensures that only the most promising varieties with proven benefits for climate resilience, nutrition, and poverty reduction continue through the breeding pipeline, optimizing resource allocation and increasing the likelihood that farmers will ultimately receive varieties that perform well under real world conditions in West Africa. The meeting involved invitation from a wide stakeholder team which included the product Design teams, where a number of key participants were invited. In the invitation gender balance was taken into considered to ensure balance.
